hook: Stuart Russell is Distinguished Professor of Computer Science at UC Berkeley, where he also holds the Smith-Zadeh Professorship in Engineering and a professorship in Cognitive Science. With Peter Norvig he co-authored Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, first published in 1995 and now in multiple editions, which became the standard textbook used to teach AI in universities worldwide. In 2016 he founded the Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI) at Berkeley, a research lab devoted to redesigning AI systems around explicit uncertainty about human preferences rather than fixed objectives, on the argument that optimizing a fixed goal too well is what makes highly capable AI systems dangerous. He set out that argument for a general audience in his 2019 book Human Compatible: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control, and in 2021 he delivered the BBC's Reith Lectures on living with artificial intelligence. He holds an OBE and is a Fellow of the Royal Society, and also serves as Professor of Computational Precision Health at UCSF and an Honorary Fellow of Wadham College, Oxford.
